working: Direct + Organic Search still carry the site: 51.1% and 33.2% of the 32,881 sessions in the trailing window, both flat vs. the 2026-09-09 run — a stable base.

The 2026-09-11 Referring Partners 'Bounce Recovery' resend still produced a real lift despite a tiny 6.94% open rate: +51.8% daily-session lift (46.3 vs 30.5 baseline) — recovery sends to a small remaining list can still move traffic.
Constant Contact connection is healthy and current: 100 campaigns synced (131 named), most recent send 2026-09-13, no auth errors on this pull.
GSC click/impression volume held roughly steady vs. last week's 7-day window (10 clicks / 1,446 impressions vs. 12 / 1,769) — no sign of a ranking drop, though see the window caveat below.
not_working: Both newsletter sends since the last report were resend/recovery variants, not fresh campaigns: 'Staff-Client eNews Aug 2026 (Non-opener resend, Sunday)' (2026-09-13, 7.71% open, 0.09% click) and 'Referring Partners eNews - August 2026 (Bounce Recovery)' (2026-09-11, 6.94% open, 0.27% click). Averaging these into cc_summary's headline rate pulled it down slightly (49.99%/1.83% vs. 50.83%/1.88% last week) — that headline now understates how original (non-resend) sends actually perform.
The 2026-09-13 non-opener resend logged a negative session lift: -25.9% (30.0 vs. 40.5 baseline) — the send window underperformed its own pre-send baseline entirely.

UTM leakage persists on the larger send: the 2026-09-11 Referring Partners resend shows direct_sessions_3d (74) outpacing email_sessions_3d (14) by 5.3x — the same historical pattern, meaning GA4 is still very likely crediting most of that traffic to Direct instead of Email.
GSC window is once again only 7 days (09-07 to 09-14), so this week's ranking numbers aren't comparable to a 30-day baseline — no genuine SEO trend call possible this cycle.
Organic Social remains marginal at 5.2% of sessions, essentially flat for the fourth straight report.
do_next: OPERATIONAL (confirmed this run): the claude-runner queue watcher skips/dedups any job whose basename has been used before, even with fresh file content — a plain 'bcc-mkt-fetch.run.ps1' drop sat unprocessed the entire poll window, and the fetch only ran once renamed to 'bcc-mkt-fetch-20260914.run.ps1'. This exact issue was already flagged in project memory on 2026-09-07 and clearly recurred on 2026-09-10 and again today. Recommend changing bcc-marketing-pulse.ps1's runner wrapper (or however the scheduled Mon/Wed cron drops its job file) to always use a date-suffixed basename so scheduled runs stop silently no-op'ing.

Add utm_source=constantcontact&utm_medium=email (plus a per-send utm_campaign) to Constant Contact templates — still the single highest-leverage fix; the 5.3x Direct-over-Email gap on the 09-11 send shows it is still not done.

Investigate the negative lift on the 09-13 non-opener resend — either the remaining non-opener list is too small/stale to move traffic, or Sunday is a poor send slot; consider testing a weekday resend instead.
Exclude resend/bounce-recovery campaign types from headline open/click rate benchmarking on the dashboard so it doesn't understate how original sends perform.
Re-run GSC on a consistent 30-day trailing window next cycle so runs become comparable again.
summary: Fresh data landed this cycle after working around the claude-runner's job-basename dedup issue (see do_next). Core traffic held steady (32,881 sessions, Direct/Organic unchanged), but the two most recent newsletter touches were both low-engagement resend/recovery variants — one with a negative session lift — and UTM leakage is still hiding real email traffic inside Direct on the larger of the two.
